Cc: sre@paylynk.com

Subject: Latency spike affecting payment validation (model v14a-quant)

Hi Stephanie,

We started seeing a sudden increase in p95 / tail latency on our payment validation API around 09:05 PST after the 03:00 rollout to v14a-quant. Error rates are stable but p95 moved from ~210ms to ~1.9s across multiple regions. This is impacting authorizations and causing timeouts in our checkout flow.

Attached are a small bundle of traces and the SLO snapshot from our monitoring: p95-traces.tar.gz, paylynk_slo_snapshot.json.

Request: Can RedWood immediately pin our traffic to the previous stable model (v13z) or authorize a rollback? We need a rapid mitigation while your team investigates. We also want any mitigations to be documented (time of change, expected impact).

Happy to jump on a call — Carlos (SRE) and our on-call PM are available now.

Thanks,
Carlos Ruiz
SRE Lead | PayLynk

---
Note: this is high-priority for our checkout flows; we may throttle traffic client-side if mitigations aren't available in the next 30 minutes.

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 10:03:30 -0800
Subject: RE: Latency spike affecting payment validation (model v14a-quant)

Stef / team — quick triage notes after looking at the traces:

- Root-cause hypothesis: regression appears in the quantized execution path for v14a-quant when serving batches with mixed sequence lengths. We see an extra kernel fallback in the scheduler (~600-800ms extra on long tails) that didn't manifest in our canary metrics (canary traffic had shorter sequence lengths).
- Impact: Elevated p95 for long-sequence requests; throughput remains stable for short sequences.
- Mitigations available now:
  1) Tenant traffic pin to v13z (previous stable) — fast change on the traffic router, ~2-5 minute propagation. Expected outcome: p95 returns to baseline. Downsides: v13z is ~10% less throughput-efficient; expect slight cost delta for PayLynk during the window.
  2) Forced routing to quantization-safe execution (we can toggle a server-side flag to avoid kernel fallback) — would require a global config flip and risk for other tenants; not recommended without broader approval.
  3) Full model rollback for PayLynk to v13z — this is effectively same as 1 but also reverts any model-config-level changes.

I can perform option 1 (tenant pin) immediately if Marissa approves. We'll follow with a postmortem and a fix job (likely a kernel scheduling patch) scheduled for the week.

Tessa Morgan
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
